ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Anti-Money Laundering (as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019); Executive Regulations of the AML Law (Presidential Decree No. 8 of 2015); Central Bank of Egypt Regulation No. 232 of 2014 regarding Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing; General Authority for Investment (GAFI) Implementing Regulations under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; and Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) directives on Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) record-keeping.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Egyptian Central Bank of Egypt sanctions and terrorism designation lists. PEP identification is compulsory under Law No. 80/2002, requiring enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. Continuous transaction monitoring and real-time screening are mandated for licensed remittance service providers under CBE Regulation No. 232/2014 and the FIU's AML/CFT supervision manual.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Portal and Company Name Clearing System (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Arabic. A transliterated or English version is permitted for commercial usage, but the Arabic transliteration must be approved by GAFI and the Commercial Registry. Latin-script names must follow the standard Egyptian transliteration rules for Arabic phonetics. Submitting a proposed name that is identical, misleadingly similar, or a direct translation of an existing registered Egyptian entity is prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a formal written appeal to the GAFI Companies Registration Legal Department within 30 days of the rejection notification. The appeal must include the proposed name, grounds for contesting the rejection, and any supporting justifications for distinctiveness. GAFI shall review and issue a final administrative decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may initiate judicial review before the Administrative Court within 60 days of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a cross-border remittance agency. A physical operational office with on-site personnel, cash handling facilities, and secure IT infrastructure in Egypt is mandatory for licensing under the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Post. Virtual office arrangements are accepted only for ancillary corporate services but not for head office or licensed activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated >70% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of registration and licensing due to the high-risk AML/CFT classification and the statutory oversight powers of CBE, GAFI, and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, principally Articles 1, 2, 4, 59-70, 74-76 and 159-161, together with its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended. Financial payment and remittance activities are additionally governed by Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, particularly the licensing provisions for payment systems, payment service providers, money transfer and foreign-exchange activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Establishment Sector and Commercial Registry Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authenticated Limited Liability Company Memorandum of Association and incorporation application submitted through the GAFI electronic incorporation service or GAFI one-stop shop, followed by Commercial Registry registration and issuance of the commercial registration certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum capital is prescribed for an ordinary Egyptian limited liability company under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. The capital must be stated in the Memorandum of Association and fully paid at incorporation. Evidence of payment or a bank certificate may be required by GAFI or the incorporation bank. No general statutory escrow account applies, but a temporary incorporation account may be required by the bank or by a sector regulator. A Central Bank-regulated remittance or payment business may be subject to separate capital, solvency, safeguarding and security requirements under its licensing framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe for and issue the quotas set out in the authenticated Memorandum of Association, with each quota fully paid in accordance with applicable Egyptian law. RESOLVED, that the Company adopt its registered office at the address recorded in the incorporation documents and authorize the Managing Director to complete any address registration, lease, tax and registry filings. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Managing Director and [Name] be appointed Authorized Signatory, each within the powers permitted by law and the Memorandum of Association. RESOLVED, that the Managing Director may open bank accounts and submit all licensing applications, subject to required regulatory approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm regulated business perimeter and founder eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), Banking Supervision and Payment Systems and Services sectors; GAFI Companies Establishment Sector
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Define whether the company will act as a payment service provider, remittance company, agent, technology provider or bank subcontractor. Do not market, receive, hold, transmit or settle customer funds before obtaining the applicable CBE authorization and any required banking or payment-system arrangements. Confirm foreign ownership, beneficial ownership, management fitness and source-of-funds requirements before filing the LLC application.
required_dossiers: Shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner identification documents
Draft Articles and Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CBE or GAFI clarification requests with a revised activity description, ownership chart or compliance memorandum. Obtain written confirmation where the proposed activity may be performed only through a licensed bank or payment service provider.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and prepare incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI electronic incorporation portal or GAFI one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select an available Arabic or bilingual company name that does not imply banking, money transfer or governmental status without authorization. Prepare the Memorandum of Association, manager appointments, registered-office evidence and powers of attorney. Legalize foreign corporate documents through the competent foreign authority, consular legalization and Egyptian authentication where required, and provide certified Arabic translations.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association and Articles
Partner passports or national identity cards
Foreign corporate certificates and constitutional documents
Board or shareholder authorization for investment
Notarized or legalized powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct name conflicts, document legalization defects, translation deficiencies or incomplete powers of attorney and resubmit through GAFI. Replace a prohibited business name or remove regulated terminology pending CBE authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and authenticate the LLC incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Establishment Sector, GAFI one-stop shop and competent notarization/authentication office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final incorporation package, pay applicable fees in Egyptian pounds, sign or authenticate the Memorandum of Association before the competent GAFI or notarization channel, and provide evidence that stated capital has been paid as required. Obtain the GAFI incorporation certificate or equivalent establishment record.
required_dossiers: Security-clearance or approval documents, if required
Power of attorney for the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure rejected signatures, missing approvals, capital evidence or notarization by filing corrected originals and obtaining a written deficiency list from GAFI. Appeal or request administrative reconsideration where a rejection is not supported by a stated legal deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company and obtain tax and labor registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office; Egyptian Tax Authority; National Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the authenticated company with the Commercial Registry and obtain the commercial registration certificate. Apply for the tax identification number and tax registration, register for value-added tax if legally required, and complete employer and social-insurance registrations before employing personnel. Establish accounting records, beneficial-owner records and statutory books.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit corrected lease, address, activity-code or tax information when queried. Obtain a tax-office inspection or written clarification where the authority disputes the registered address or VAT classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt governance resolutions and operational controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management, GAFI where filings are required, Egyptian Tax Authority and applicable CBE supervisory channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first managers' or partners' meeting, approve quota subscriptions, registered office, bank mandates, accounting policies, delegation limits and compliance functions. Maintain minutes, partner registers, manager records and beneficial-owner information. Appoint compliance, money-laundering reporting and information-security officers where required by the CBE license or payment-service framework.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt supplemental resolutions, correct authority limits and update GAFI, banks or CBE records. Suspend affected operations until missing compliance appointments or controls are implemented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for CBE payment and remittance authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Egypt, Payment Systems and Services sector and relevant licensing committee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed licensing application for the precise service model, including local cash-pickup arrangements and any SWIFT-related activity. Provide the business plan, governance, capital and financial projections, AML/CFT program, customer due diligence procedures, safeguarding and settlement model, technology architecture, cybersecurity controls, outsourcing agreements, agent network controls and fit-and-proper information. Execute agreements only with appropriately licensed banks, payment systems or other approved counterparties.
required_dossiers: Detailed business plan and three-year financial projections
Audited or certified financial information, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the CBE licensing channel to information requests, amend the business model or submit a revised control framework. Do not commence the regulated activity while the application is pending. Preserve written records of any refusal and pursue the applicable administrative grievance or judicial review route.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Egypt for remittance and payment services; General Authority for Investment and Free Zones for company and investment formalities; local authority for premises licensing. The activity is financial services and is not an industrial manufacturing activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Central Bank of Egypt license for payment services, payment-system participation or money-transfer/remittance activity, as applicable to the approved business model

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a full EIA for a standard office-based financial-services operation with no manufacturing, industrial emissions or process wastewater. The competent environmental authority may require screening, environmental approval or site-specific conditions if the premises include material equipment, generators, construction or other potentially polluting activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial VOC discharge is permitted from an ordinary remittance office. Any wastewater discharge, air emissions from generators, hazardous materials or waste must comply with Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended, its Executive Regulations, and Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020. Hazardous electronic, battery and generator waste must be segregated and transferred through authorized contractors; noise, fuel storage and generator emissions require applicable local approvals and operating controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain premises approval and fire-safety certification from the competent Civil Protection authority before opening to the public. Maintain approved exits, fire detection and extinguishing systems, emergency lighting, evacuation plans and electrical safety controls. Obtain landlord and local-authority approvals for structural alterations, signage and maximum occupancy; conduct structural-load and electrical inspections where required. Comply with applicable occupational health and safety requirements under Egyptian Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, as amended, including workplace risk assessments, training, first aid and incident records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; official self-service portal: eta.gov.eg and e-invoicing system: einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a Tax Card (TIN) by submitting the incorporation certificate, power of attorney, passport copies of directors, lease or proof of local establishment, and a completed ETA registration application; registration is completed through the ETA one-stop shop with subsequent electronic VAT ID activation via the ETA e-invoicing portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Egyptian tax law; taxation is fixed at entity level for LLCs. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized; alignment with domestic entity characterization is mandatory for treaty and VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies; mandatory VAT registration upon exceeding the threshold, with voluntary registration permitted below it
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B transactions require e-invoicing with real-time fiscal clearance via the ETA's API; each invoice must be digitally signed and transmitted within 24 hours; B2C e-receipts are mandatory for eligible traders; QR code stamping is required on simplified invoices and receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported physical goods and qualifying international services, including cross-border remittance processing services provided to non-residents, are zero-rated subject to documentary proof that the goods or services left Egypt's territorial scope and were supplied to a recipient outside Egypt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate confirming foreign currency receipt
Bank transfer credit note evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to ETA audit covering export records, forex receipts, and supporting contracts; false or unsupported zero-rating triggers VAT assessment at 14%, additional late penalties up to 100% of tax due, and administrative fines ranging from EGP 50,000 to EGP 5,000,000; fraud cases may impose criminal penalties and full clawback with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary authority and foreign-exchange regulator under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank Law) and Law No. 88 of 2003 (Bank and Credit Law). CBE operates the Foreign Exchange Trading System (FETS) and supervises all currency and payment operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed-float exchange-rate regime for EGP. Current-account transactions (trade in goods and services) are generally convertible without prior licence. Capital-account transactions (profit repatriation, dividend distribution, intercompany loans, and investment liquidation) require documentary proof of underlying commercial purpose, CBE registration of foreign investment, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and compliance with CBE Circular No. 25/2016 (as amended). Repatriation of profits by an EG_LLC is permitted only after the annual audit is filed with GAFI and the relevant tax authorities; funds must be remitted through an authorised bank in the original currency or converted at the prevailing market rate. For remittance-service fees classified as invisibles, CBE reporting thresholds apply and the full amount of collected foreign currency must be credited to the company's licensed account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current CBE regulations, proceeds from exports of goods must be repatriated to Egypt through an authorised bank within 180 days from shipment date unless an extension is approved; for services (including money transmission commissions) the applicable receipt window is 90 days from service completion. There is no mandatory forced conversion ratio in Egypt since the 2016 FX liberalisation; however, 100% of the export/remittance value must be received into the Egyptian banking system. For a remittance agent, incoming cross-border settlement flows must be credited to the designated CBE-licensed collection account and reported through the electronic transfer system on a same-day basis. Residual EGP balances from conversion are subject to CBE liquidity-management guidelines, and any failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline triggers a compliance review and potential fines.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Account in EGP and USD/EUR with sweep facility
Operational Account with SWIFT and mobile-wallet interoperability; Capital Escrow Account for CBE licensing deposit
Multi-currency Operational Account; dedicated FX hedging derivative account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: LOW to MEDIUM. Off-shore fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer) do not hold a CBE electronic payment-service-provider (PSP) licence and therefore cannot act as the primary settlement gateway for Egypt-domiciled remittance flows. They may be used only for ancillary supplier payments where a local regulated bank account remains the principal treasury vehicle. Legal constraints under CBE payment regulations mandate that all Egypt inbound and outbound transaction settlement must pass through a licensed bank or a CBE-approved sub-processor; non-bank entities do not have direct SWIFT access. A licensed local electronic payment company may be engaged as a technical rails aggregator, but the core custody of client funds must remain with a commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence: Mandatory in-person KYC interview for at least one director or authorised signatory before the bank's compliance officer is essential for this high-risk licence category. Remote opening is permissible in principle for non-resident directors under a notarised power of attorney granted to a resident authorised representative, provided the POA is apostilled or legally certified in the director's home jurisdiction and accepted by the bank's AML committee. In practice, tier-1 banks in Egypt require a physical visit to the branch by the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or senior executive at onboarding stage; failure to do so materially delays account activation. A clear internal policy mandating in-person due diligence is recommended to accelerate the onboarding timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Categorised as a specialised money remitter under the high-risk AML sector covered by Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 and its executive regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE remittance-licence or written confirmation of pending application; independent AML compliance manual; board resolution appointing a qualified Money-Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO); documented customer risk-assessment matrix; CDD/KYC template files; staff training record logs; sample transaction-monitoring and sanction-screening reports; internal audit certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or complex ownership chain obscuring the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO); the bank will flag insufficient transparency for a regulated remittance entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chamber-certified constitutional documents of EG_LLC; notarised and legalised share register and ownership tree down to natural persons; passport copies and proof of address for each UBO; resident agent POA; certificate of good standing from the entity's home registry; sworn UBO self-declaration; completed bank-specific beneficial-ownership forms; corporate registry extract from GAFI.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows involving high-risk corridors (e.g., GCC, North Africa, and conflict zones) trigger intense sanctions and terror-financing screening, potentially freezing payment settlements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening policy using updated OFAC, UN, EU, and local consolidated lists, with server logs; source-of-funds declarations for every remittance batch; customer risk rating matrix; remittance contract packs and supporting trade documentation; internal audit reports; records of CTR and STR filings to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); post-transaction reconciliation statements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections (share capital, shareholder loans, and licence contributions) must be remitted via SWIFT to the company's CBE-licensed bank account. The overseas remitter must include the appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'ECUR' for equity capital) and the bank will verify economic substance against the investment registration certificate issued by GAFI or the relevant supervisory authority. For remittance agents, settlement funds from overseas correspondents must be credited to the designated collection account and reconciled with CBE's electronic transfer reporting portal on a trade-date basis. Cash funding is strictly prohibited; bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation is mandatory and must be supported by an indemnity covering source of funds and purpose of the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operating disbursements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for all cross-border bank transfers. Local cash-pickup settlements will be executed through the CBE Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system and the Egyptian inter-bank mobile wallet platform (InstaPay) for last-mile distribution. Commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) are opened through the same corporate bank using UCP600 standard rules and require pro-forma invoices, certificates of origin, and customs declarations where applicable. All outbound foreign-currency payments must be filed with CBE within the prescribed reporting period and meet the underlying business-activity test; supporting contracts and tax-compliance certificates (e.g., withholding tax receipts) must be maintained on file for four years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright forwards (FX forwards) in EGP/USD and EGP/EUR - executed with authorised banks only after demonstrating a genuine underlying remittance or trade exposure, documented by contract and forecast cash flow.
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) - permissible for liquidity and treasury management when paired with a corresponding commercial transaction, subject to CBE compliance and reporting obligations.
Exchange-traded FX futures on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) - available for EGP/USD hedging with approved local brokerage counterparties, subject to position limits.

Option contracts (calls and puts on EGP) - may be offered by qualified banks to corporate clients with approved treasury policies; must be settled physically and cannot be used for speculative purposes.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - not generally permitted for onshore Egyptian corporates; only non-resident counterparties with CBE-approved hedging programmes may access NDFs through international banks, and any settlement involving an Egyptian entity requires prior central-bank approval and subsequent reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements approved by the shareholders' meeting and filed with the Companies Registry under GAFI supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine under the Companies Law; persistent default exposes the LLC to an administrative warning, repeated penalties, and strike-off from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the tax period (by 30 April for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency penalty of 2% per month or part month on unpaid tax under Law 91/2005; non-filing can trigger estimated assessment and criminal prosecution for evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation and UBO register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the commercial registry declaration, and within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update UBO information is subject to administrative fines and suspension of voting or dividend rights; severe breach enables strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of payment-service and remittance authorization issued by the Central Bank of Egypt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submission no later than 30 days before the stated expiry date of the CBE license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal results in license suspension or revocation, prohibition of remittance operations, and monetary penalties under the Banking Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal and maintenance filing for the LLC establishment record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry affiliated with GAFI and the Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the anniversary of original registration or by the annual renewal cycle specified on the registry certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs daily late fees and possible administrative delisting; continued nonrenewal enables the registry to strike off the entity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All licensed cross-border remittance operators are subject to mandatory annual audit as a CBE licensing condition; additionally, audit is statutorily required when ETA or GAFI thresholds for turnover, assets, or shareholder capital are exceeded
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which align with IFRS, as adopted for companies regulated by GAFI and the CBE

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must annually confirm the beneficial ownership schedule in the commercial registry declaration, record any shareholding transfers in the UBO register, and notify GAFI and the AML FIU within 30 days of a transfer or other UBO change

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic reduction for financial services. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may allow an income deduction of up to 50% of taxable profits for up to 7 years for eligible projects in underdeveloped governorates or strategic sectors, subject to ministerial approval and actual investment substance. The general LLC rate remains 22.5%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority Form No. 7 (Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Persons), submitted electronically through the ETA e-filing portal (eta.gov.eg / tax.gov.eg). E-invoicing support must also be maintained through the Rased platform for all commercial invoices.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional tax payment instalments due by the end of the month following each quarter)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year. For calendar-year LLCs, the statutory deadline is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from cross-border remittance services, transaction fees, commissions, exchange spreads, and ancillary payment processing income, net of discounts and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned LLC must report all Egypt-source revenue from cross-border money transmission on an accrual basis, including income cleared through SWIFT and local cash pickup rails.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct and indirect expenses: payroll, bank charges, SWIFT costs, cash pooling fees, regulatory licence amortisation, rent, utility costs, insurance, and depreciation determined under Egyptian tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident affiliates are deductible only where supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, beneficial ownership evidence, and proof of withholding tax deposit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Net Taxable Income / Tax Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-adjusted profit after adding back non-deductible amounts, applying special deductions, and deducting carryforward tax losses (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC reports a loss, the loss certificate must be retained. Carryforward relief is limited to 5 years and cannot be claimed against branch profits unless a treaty provides otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all transactions with related parties, including nature, volume, pricing method, and economic substance, as required under Egyptian transfer pricing rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled LLCs with related-party transactions exceeding EGP 8 million must attach Local File/Master File and obtain ETA acknowledgement before filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed penalty of EGP 1,000 plus a monthly surcharge of 2% of tax due (minimum EGP 500), capped at 40% of assessed tax. Underpayment penalties apply to omitted tax. Material false declarations may expose criminal tax evasion sanctions with imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced or nil DTA rate on dividend repatriation, the non-resident recipient must deliver to the Egyptian payer: (i) an in-effect Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, (ii) a completed DTA relief declaration/consolidated ETA letter, and (iii) a beneficiary ownership statement. The Egyptian payer must generally withhold at the statutory 10% rate and apply to ETA for refund or obtain pre-approval for treaty exemption. ETA typically issues advance treaty clearance within 30 business days of complete submissions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest on loans 20%, royalties for IP use 20%, and management/technical service fees 20% when paid to non-residents. Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction; e.g., under many Egyptian DTAs interest is reduced to 5–15% and royalties to 0–15%, subject to beneficial ownership and active business substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8 million aggregate annual value of related-party transactions triggers mandatory TP disclosure, Local File and Master File preparation. A Master File is also required where the MNE group records consolidated revenue above EGP 350 million. Egypt applies CbCR notification thresholds consistent with OECD base erosion rules for large groups.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the ETA applies substance-over-form principles, CFC provisions, and anti-abuse doctrines to disregard shell LLCs. A remittance LLC must maintain premises, staff, independent management, board minutes, bank accounts, and transaction decision-making within Egypt to evidence real economic activity and obtain treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of Egypt-source remittance revenue, laundering fees through offshore shell entities, fabricating expenses, or failing to issue invoices on the Rased e-invoicing platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 91 of 2005, articles 133–135: imprisonment up to 3 years, a fine of EGP 1,000 to EGP 5,000 or up to twice the evaded tax, and payment of all evaded tax plus penalties (up to 100%). Criminal prosecution may be brought before the Economic Offences Court.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties if the corporate veil is pierced. Travel bans, asset freezes, and seizure of personal property may be imposed, with imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Egyptian LLC as a conduit for pass-through remittance flows with no real employees, office, board decisions, or independent capital; claiming treaty relief without substantive local activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the LLC, recharacterise the activities of the foreign parent or shareholder, recapture withholding tax, impose deficiency assessments, and revoke the company's remittance licence under Law No. 72 of 2017.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held responsible for the entire tax deficiency under veil-lifting; criminal liability may attach for assisting a sham arrangement, leading to travel bans, disqualification, and imprisonment for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing cross-border remittance rails without enforceable customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or the special licence required under Law No. 80 of 2002 and Central Bank of Egypt rules; processing illicit funds through cash pickup networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: License revocation, administrative fines starting from EGP 200,000 per violation, forfeiture of funds, and suspension from clearing and settlement systems. Criminal AML conviction can result in imprisonment up to 7 years and fines up to EGP 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management are personally liable for deliberate or negligent failure to file STRs/CDD under AML law. Personal bank accounts may be frozen; directors may face travel bans, strikes-off from the commercial register, and imprisonment of up to 7 years.
